summary: Flinders Island Airport (FLS) is a small regional airport located near Whitemark, serving the Furneaux Group of islands in the eastern Bass Strait off the northeast tip of Tasmania. It functions as the primary aviation gateway for residents and visitors traveling to Flinders Island, a remote destination renowned for its rugged coastline, abundant wildlife, and uncrowded beaches. The airport handles a handful of daily turboprop services connecting the island with mainland Tasmania and Victoria.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Flinders Island Airport?
A: Sharp Airlines and Regional Express (Rex) operate regular scheduled services to Flinders Island, primarily connecting Whitemark with Melbourne (Essendon) and Launceston in Tasmania.

Q: How far is the airport from Whitemark town centre?
A: The airport is located only a few kilometres south of Whitemark, making it a quick drive of around five minutes into the main township.

Q: Are there car rental services at Flinders Island Airport?
A: Yes, local car rental operators offer pickup services at the airport, and booking in advance is strongly recommended as vehicle availability can be limited, especially in peak season.

Q: Does the airport operate at night?
A: No, Flinders Island Airport has limited operating hours and does not provide night-time services, so flights are scheduled during daylight hours only.
transport_tips: Renting a car at Flinders Island Airport is the most practical way to explore the island, as public transport is minimal and many of the best beaches and nature reserves are spread across remote areas. Local taxi operators can be arranged in advance for transfers to Whitemark or surrounding accommodation. Travellers should plan fuel stops carefully, as services on the island are limited and distances between attractions can be deceptively long on winding rural roads.
local_tip: Bring binoculars and a wildlife checklist — Flinders Island is part of the Furneaux Group, home to the rare Cape Barren goose, short-tailed shearwater colonies, and wombat populations you may spot from roadside verges, especially around dusk.
